## Description

The description the MCP server sends to the model, word for word. Its rules apply to every call.

> Generate one animated GIF and get back its url. Use it when the user asks for a GIF or an animation. Describe the motion beat by beat and say it should loop. Pick 4 to 6 frames for a simple motion, 8 to 12 for smoother motion. To put it on a note, pass the url as imageUrl to create_note, create_many_notes or update_note. A GIF counts as one image against the user's weekly Coach usage. It cannot edit an existing image; use generate_image for that.

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aspect` | `string` | No | square for notes and most posts. portrait for phone-first posts. landscape for article headers. One of: `"square"`, `"portrait"`, `"landscape"`. Default `"square"`. |
| `frameDurationMs` | `integer` | No | How long each frame shows, in milliseconds. 80 to 150 for smooth motion, 300 to 800 for a slow slideshow. Min 40. Max 1000. Default `150`. |
| `frames` | `integer` | No | How many frames, 2 to 12. 4 to 6 for a simple blink or bounce, 8 to 12 for smoother motion. Min 2. Max 12. Default `8`. |
| `prompt` | `string` | Yes | What the GIF shows and how it moves, start to end: subject, style, colors, the motion in each beat, and that it loops smoothly. Spell any text exactly. Min length 3. Max length 4000. |
| `quality` | `string` | No | low for most GIFs. medium when it has text or fine detail. One of: `"low"`, `"medium"`. Default `"low"`. |
